verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y wins narrowly on three verified, material differences. (1) Key item k14: Y is the only output that actually describes the assignee oracle's mechanism (agent_assignee_argv walks up to CC_WF_MAX_HOPS:-8 ancestors at hooks/lib/agent-identity.sh:46 requiring the three-flag conjunction at :53, cross-confirmed trichotomously by agent_team_member_confirms at :93-124 with the exact rc semantics) — I verified every line; X only names the functions and an rc-0/2 rule, and mis-ranges the function as :33-62 when it is :33-77. (2) The brief mandates the ledger rung as part of trigger predicate (a); Y grounds it in code I verified (DIRTY at wrap-ledger.sh:527-529, UNLANDED at :532-539, ⛔ precedence at :1972-1973, 'Land IN FLIGHT' at :1985-1986, 🚀 at :1997-1998 and :2053-2056), while X explicitly says it did not read wrap-ledger at all. (3) Y produces a second, verified differing-default pair the key does not name — session-continue.sh:420 `${CC_PANE_ID:-${ITERM_SESSION_ID:-}}` versus session-register.sh:134 `${CC_PANE_ID:-${ITERM_SESSION_ID:-${KITTY_WINDOW_ID:-}}}` — plus verified extras X lacks (`.ship` survives `clear`; window_end max 0 means no window cap; the legacy mailbox_take path consumes before the emit). X's counterweights are real — its stale-citation audit is the deepest and I confirmed every item, including the substantive finding that wf_teardown_marked is NOT 'verbatim' from lead-crash-watchdog's classify_death (the watchdog additionally requires `\"mode\":\"teardown\"` and `find -mmin -30` at :257-258) — but X also carries four bad citations (KILL_RE at :349 not :348, mailbox-drain.sh:224 is `fi` not a mailbox_take_n call, agent-identity ranges) against Y's two harmless range overshoots, and Y's own audit (5 stale + 4 accurate) checked out completely.

X vs Z — X wins narrowly. The decisive verified differences: (1) the key's own PRECISION NOTE on k10 says $cust is NOT 'rows attributed to this pane'; X states it exactly (cust = cust_mine + cust_unk at :758, with the :762-764 fallback counting every row as unknown, so a sibling's unattributable row keeps the floor re-firing), while Z glosses the predicate as 'attributable open dispatched work' and never says cust_unk enters it. (2) Z carries a material wrong claim of precisely the class the brief warns about — that session_dirty_mine canonicalises BOTH sides through _sw_canon; in fact only the transcript side does (:293-299), the git side being `abs=\"$top/$rel\"` at :332, and Z appears to have repeated session_unlanded_mine's comment at :372 instead of reading session_dirty_mine's body. (3) Z asserts the CC_MECH_MAX split is 'non-hazardous' and that an explicit override 'makes the two sites agree'; X found the real holes (different processes, and `clear`'s sid at :260 versus the arm's stdin sid at :1060 making the spend a no-op). Z also fabricates the symbol `sha1sum` where the code calls `shasum` (:25), and contradicts itself in Q2 about when the armed path is reached. Z's genuine advantages — the fold sitting after the kill-switch and CAP exits so those Stops never surface mail, the ship-floor-vs-wake-floor payload shape asymmetry (:1197 vs :892-893), and the correct 🔧 = DIRTY-or-REMAINDER decomposition X never read — are real and verified, but they do not outweigh one substantive wrong mechanism claim plus the missed key precision, especially against the brief's explicit demand to ground claims in code rather than comments, which is the axis X is strongest on and Z is weakest on.

Y vs Z — Y wins. Y has the full k14 mechanism that Z reduces to two function names and an rc rule; Y states the k10 precision (cust = mine + unknown, with the no-pane-id fallback) that Z's 'attributable' gloss misses; Y's session-writes account is correct where Z's is wrong (Z claims both sides of session_dirty_mine's intersection pass through _sw_canon — refuted at :332); Y produces a verified second differing-default pair (session-register.sh:134's KITTY_WINDOW_ID tier, absent from session-continue.sh:420) where Z asserts, with a grep it describes but whose scope excludes this case, that every other budget has exactly one default; and Y's citation audit is both larger and fully verified (5 stale, 4 accurate) against Z's two confirmations plus a list of files it declined to open. Z's unique verified insights (fold-after-cap/kill-switch, payload-shape asymmetry, the 🔧 ladder decomposition, two hooks blocking on one Stop) are genuine and I credited them, but Y matches or exceeds Z on ledger grounding and carries only one incomplete gloss (presenting DIRTY=1 as the sole 🔧 source) against Z's fabricated symbol, wrong canonicalisation claim, and internal Q2 inconsistency.
